title: Sixi Assure architecture model
description: Typed graph model (docs/02). Single source of truth; Go validation and Zod schemas derive from this file. Invariants that JSON Schema cannot express are listed in $comment and enforced in the model package.
$comment: Server-enforced invariants (docs/02 §4): (1) edge endpoints reference existing node ids; (2) no self-loops except agent→agent 'delegates' with auth=obo; (3) a node belongs to at most one zone group (node.zone must match the zone group listing it) and may belong to many trust boundaries; (4) source=observed nodes are read-only; (5) region attrs must be known Azure regions or a generic region code; (6) findings and evidence reference existing ids; (7) ids are unique across nodes, edges, groups, findings and identities; (8) a node's attrs.identity_id names an entry of identities[] and an identity's registry names an agent_registry node (schema 1.1); (9) every provenance key resolves to a model element, member or attribute, and the sidecar is written by the server alone (ADR-086, schema 1.1); (10) an agent's or agent_memory's attrs.hosted_on names another existing node (schema 1.2, ADR-093 SD-2); (11) an edge attribute annotated 'x-edge-kinds' is set only on an edge of those kinds and a group attribute annotated 'x-group-kinds' only on a group of those kinds (schema 1.2: the delegation attributes on delegates, the flow-group attributes on flows, the workflow bounds on workflow groups). 'x-required-attrs' lists attributes that must be completed for inventory purposes — their absence is reported by rules (e.g. AI-005), not rejected by validation. 'x-required-unless' (schema 1.1) names a required attribute another declared attribute replaces: an agent that declares identity_id no longer needs the deprecated identity string. 'x-attr-values' (schema 1.1) narrows an attribute the flat nodeAttrs set shares between types to the values one type accepts (e.g. gateway.kind vs agent_registry.kind, edge_device egress_policy boolean vs agent egress_policy enum); enforced in Go.

schema_version.description: Schema version the model follows (ADR-040 §1, docs/02 §Versions), MAJOR.MINOR. Optional on input: a model without it is 0.9 and is upgraded on read; the server writes the current version whenever it saves or returns a model.
schema_version.$comment: MINOR adds optional attributes, enum values or node types; MAJOR renames or removes. Older versions are upgraded on read by the model package/migrate, never validated against this file.

identities.$comment: ADR-047 §1 (schema 1.1): identities as entities. Nodes reference one by attrs.identity_id; the model holds claims about an identity, never a credential (credential_ttl is a duration, ref an identifier; the secret guard scans every string).

noteTone.$comment: ADR-081: the colour of a note; absent means neutral

regionCode.$comment: validated against the Azure region list plus generic codes (eu, us, ch, uk, global, unknown) in Go

capabilities.$comment: Declared capability classes of a tool or MCP server (docs/02 §3). Design-time declaration by the architect, never observed.

integrity.$comment: How the tool or MCP server definition is fixed against later change (rug pull).

evaluationScope.$comment: What an evaluation node is declared to cover (docs/02 §3). A design-time declaration of scope; results are never recorded here.

edgeProtocol.$comment: ADR-047 §2 (schema 1.1): the protocol of an edge, an enum so rules can reason about it. Free text from 1.0 is mapped by the 1.0 → 1.1 migration (known spellings lowercased, anything else → other with attrs.x_migrated_from) and stays readable for two MINOR versions (docs/02 §Versions).

federation.$comment: How the identity obtains its credential: a federated exchange (workload identity federation, SPIFFE, Entra Agent ID, an OIDC client) or a static key.

sandbox.$comment: ADR-047 §3 for mcp_server (none/process/container/os_sandbox) amended by docs/18 D3 with managed for an agent on a managed platform and by ADR-093 FS-08 (schema 1.2) for a tool: wasm (a WebAssembly guest), vm (a micro-VM or gVisor), model_hosted (the model provider runs the code); the per-type values are in x-attr-values.

securitySchemes.$comment: A2A agent card securitySchemes, as declared on the card (docs/research/06 §27).

humanInTheLoop.$comment: ADR-047 §3: per tool class, what the agent does before acting: ask a person, defer to a person, or never act.

framework.$comment: ADR-093 FS-01 (schema 1.2): the agent framework the agent is built with; M4 chooses the framework-native remediation sentence by it.

orchestration.$comment: ADR-093 FS-03 (schema 1.2): the multi-agent pattern an orchestrating agent runs (LangGraph supervisor and swarm, MAF builders, ADK shell agents, CrewAI processes).

guardrails.$comment: ADR-093 FS-15 (schema 1.2): the checks around the agent's model and tool calls, per stage: written as code, judged by an LLM, a platform policy (e.g. Foundry rai_config) or information-flow labels; blocking stops the run; scope runner applies to every agent the runner hosts. content_safety stays the fact AI-002 and AGT-003 read.

hostedProtocols.$comment: ADR-093 FS-19 (schema 1.2): what a hosted agent runtime serves (LangGraph Server /mcp and /a2a, Foundry agent endpoint protocols, MAF hosted protocols, ADK api_server --a2a).

ref.$comment: an identifier (object id, client id, SPIFFE ID), never a credential

issuer.$comment: who issues the credential: an issuer URL or the name of the identity provider

credential_ttl.$comment: lifetime of one issued credential, in seconds

rotation_days.$comment: ADR-047 §3b identity.rotation: days between rotations of a long-lived credential

blueprint.$comment: Entra Agent ID blueprint (or another platform's template) the identity is created from

registry.$comment: id of the agent_registry node the identity is registered in (checked in Go)

trust_domain.$comment: SPIFFE trust domain or tenant the identity belongs to

identity.$comment: ADR-047 §1 (schema 1.1). Ids share the namespace of nodes, edges, groups and findings.

sponsor.$comment: schema 1.1: the person accountable for the system on the business side (ADR-089)

substantial_modification.$comment: docs/03 §MR: whether the AI command path is a substantial modification of the machinery it acts on (Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Art. 3(16), 18), as assessed with the risk assessment

extValue.$comment: x_ attrs are free-form scalars (max 2000 chars for strings)

max_iterations.$comment: ADR-093 FS-06: superstep or loop bound of the workflow; absent = undeclared, 0 = unbounded

checkpointing.$comment: ADR-093 FS-06: where the workflow checkpoints its state between steps

retention_days.$comment: days data is kept; on an agent_memory (schema 1.2, ADR-093 FS-11) 0 = never expires

purpose.$comment: free text on agents, llm endpoints, evaluations and SaaS; log_sink (schema 1.1): operational, security or evidence — per-type values in x-attr-values

kind.$comment: gateway: api, ai, waf, mcp, a2a, egress; agent_registry (schema 1.1): mcp, agent365, api_center, gemini_enterprise, custom, and foundry (schema 1.2, ADR-093 FS-24); agent (schema 1.2, ADR-093 FS-02): llm (has a model of its own) or orchestrator (routes without one) — per-type values in x-attr-values

encryption_key.$comment: platform- or customer-managed key; none (schema 1.2, ADR-093 FS-12) = the store does not encrypt at rest

row_level_security.$comment: docs/03 §OT: the store enforces row-level security per caller context (e.g. SESSION_CONTEXT per OT zone)

gamp_category.$comment: docs/03 §GXP: GAMP software category of this component (1 infrastructure, 3 non-configured, 4 configured, 5 custom); categories 3-5 are a continuum, not a checklist

supplier_assessed.$comment: docs/03 §GXP: the supplier of this component, or the team that built it, has been assessed (GAMP 5 Appendix M2) and the assessment is on file

safety_function.$comment: docs/03 §MR: the component performs or ensures a safety function of machinery

self_evolving.$comment: docs/03 §MR: fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning, i.e. it keeps learning after being placed on the market or put into service

conformity_route.$comment: docs/03 §MR: the conformity assessment procedure applied (Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Art. 25): internal production control (A), EU type-examination + conformity to type (B+C), full quality assurance (H), unit verification (G)

intervention_log.$comment: docs/03 §MR: the node records evidence of every intervention in the machine (commands, software, configuration) in a tracing log kept five years

egress_policy.$comment: edge_device/edge_gateway: a fail-closed egress allow-list exists (boolean); agent (schema 1.1): default_deny_allowlist, default_allow or undeclared; tool (schema 1.2, ADR-093 FS-09): the same values plus disabled (executed code reaches no network) — per-type values in x-attr-values

command_validation.$comment: docs/03 §OT: this node validates every command before it acts on a machine (signature, freshness, nonce, allow-list, range, state)

approval_identity.$comment: docs/03 §OT: the identity an approval is signed under; separate = the approver's own, distinct from the agent's and the executor's

exposure.$comment: app/api: internal, public, unknown; mcp_server (schema 1.1): loopback, private_network, public — per-type values in x-attr-values

authn.$comment: ADR-047 §3b (schema 1.1): every authentication method the app or API accepts. A single 1.0 value is migrated to a one-item list and stays readable for two MINOR versions.

key_use.$comment: docs/03 §OT: what a secret store's keys are for; command_signing keys authorise machine commands

c4_parent.$comment: ADR-032: id of the containing SoftwareSystem/Container element (C4 parent); empty = top level

hosted_on.$comment: docs/02 §3: id of the node this component runs on (same host or process); calls between co-located nodes need no transport encryption. Schema 1.2 (ADR-093 FS-14, SD-2): also on an agent (the app or runtime it runs in) and an agent_memory (the store it lives in), where it must name another existing node (checked in Go)

provider_service.$comment: ADR-032: provider service slug, e.g. azure/aks, azure/openai

text.$comment: ADR-081: the words of a note (required and non-empty on a note, checked in Go); the secret guard applies

identity_id.$comment: ADR-047 §1: id of the identities[] entry this component runs as (checked in Go)

sponsor.$comment: ADR-047 §3: the person accountable for the agent (Entra Agent ID sponsor)

inbound_auth.$comment: ADR-047 §3: the scheme the agent accepts from its callers

card_signed.$comment: A2A: the agent card carries a signature

egress_allowlist.$comment: hosts or services the agent (or, schema 1.2, the code a tool executes) may reach when egress_policy is default_deny_allowlist

hosting.$comment: docs/18 D3: the agent runs on infrastructure the organisation operates or on a managed agent platform

spec_version.$comment: MCP specification revision the server implements, e.g. 2026-07-28

transport.$comment: MCP transport (http_sse is the deprecated HTTP+SSE transport; websocket, schema 1.2, ADR-093 FS-16)

auth_mode.$comment: how the MCP server authenticates its clients

resource_metadata.$comment: the MCP server publishes OAuth protected resource metadata (RFC 9728)

client_registration.$comment: how MCP clients register: client ID metadata document, pre-registration, or dynamic client registration

registry_entry.$comment: name of the server's entry in an MCP registry

cache_scope.$comment: CacheableResult scope: public means shared gateways may cache list/read results

functions.$comment: ADR-047 §3: what the gateway enforces, so 'a gateway on the path' is answered per function

write_path.$comment: agent_memory: what writes into the memory (free text from the framework, e.g. every_step, add_session_to_memory)

validated.$comment: agent_memory: content is validated before it is written

scope.$comment: agent_memory: who shares the memory; tenant (schema 1.2, ADR-093 FS-10) = every user and agent of one tenant

verification.$comment: agent_registry: how entries are verified before listing

trust_anchor.$comment: agent_registry: the key entries and cards are verified against, and when it was fetched

issues.$comment: credential_broker: what the broker hands out

max_lifetime.$comment: credential_broker: longest lifetime of an issued credential, in seconds

holds_credentials.$comment: datastore: the store also keeps a credential at rest

data_classes.$comment: every class of data the component holds, beside the single data_class

input_guard.$comment: app/api: an ingestion guard inspects inbound content (ADR-041)

retention_statement.$comment: llm_endpoint: the provider's statement on prompt and output retention (ADR-043 §3): who asserted it, when, and where it is published

form.$comment: product: the form the product is placed on the market in

secrets_delivery.$comment: how secrets reach the process (secrets_in says where they are stored)

environment.$comment: deployment environment of the component; shared = serves more than one

redundancy.$comment: how the component survives a zone or region loss (zonal = one zone)

region_name.$comment: the provider-qualified region beside the validated region code, e.g. gcp/europe-west6

framework_version.$comment: ADR-093 FS-01: the framework release the agent is built with, e.g. 1.0.3

max_iterations.$comment: ADR-093 FS-04/FS-06: loop bound of an agent (or, on a workflow group, of the workflow); absent = undeclared, 0 = unbounded

max_tool_calls.$comment: ADR-093 FS-04: tool calls one run may make; absent = undeclared, 0 = unbounded

max_duration_s.$comment: ADR-093 FS-04: longest run, in seconds; absent = undeclared, 0 = unbounded

definition_source.$comment: ADR-093 FS-21: where the agent definition is loaded from (repository = fetched from a remote repository at load time)

config_imports_code.$comment: ADR-093 FS-21: loading the declarative definition imports code it names (ADK YAML, stdio commands launched at load)

config_env_access.$comment: ADR-093 FS-21: expressions in the definition can read the environment (MAF PowerFx with safe_mode off)

encryption.$comment: agent_memory (schema 1.2, ADR-093 FS-12): how stored state is encrypted: not at all, by the application before it is written, or by the store at rest

deserialization.$comment: agent_memory (schema 1.2, ADR-093 FS-13): whether stored state is turned back into code objects when it is read

invoked_from.$comment: mcp_server (schema 1.2, ADR-093 FS-17): who opens the MCP connection: the agent's process, or the model provider (a hosted MCP tool, so the server must be reachable from the provider)

sampling.$comment: mcp_server (schema 1.2, ADR-093 FS-18): whether the server may ask the agent's model for completions

note.$comment: ADR-081: an annotation outside assessment; no rule, inventory or C4 view reads it

agent_memory.$comment: ADR-047 §3 (schema 1.1): what an agent remembers across turns or sessions; schema 1.2 (ADR-093 FS-10 to FS-14) adds its encryption, deserialisation and the store it is hosted_on

agent_registry.$comment: ADR-047 §3 (schema 1.1): a registry agents, MCP servers or cards are listed in

credential_broker.$comment: ADR-047 §3 (schema 1.1): a token vault or credential provider that holds credentials instead of the agent

external_agent.$comment: ADR-047 §3 (schema 1.1): an A2A peer outside the organisation's control, described by its card

audience.$comment: ADR-047 §1: the audience (resource indicator) the token on this call is issued for

token_binding.$comment: ADR-047 §1: sender constraint of the token (none = bearer)

token_lifetime.$comment: ADR-047 §1: lifetime of the token on this call, in seconds

scopes.$comment: ADR-047 §1: scopes the token on this call carries

delegation_depth.$comment: ADR-047 §1: how many delegations deep the call's authority is (0 = the caller's own)

consent.$comment: ADR-047 §1: the consent the delegated token rests on

guarded.$comment: ADR-047 §3b: the write path passes an ingestion guard (ADR-041 secret guard or equivalent)

mode.$comment: ADR-093 FS-05 (SD-1): as_tool = the caller keeps control and gets a result; handoff = control transfers to the target

routing.$comment: ADR-093 FS-05: whether code or the model chooses this hop

bidirectional.$comment: ADR-093 FS-05: the target may hand control back (or on) to the caller

context_forwarded.$comment: ADR-093 FS-05: what of the conversation the target sees

flow_group.$comment: ADR-093 FS-07: edge-group semantics of a flows edge between the executors of a workflow

condition_name.$comment: ADR-093 FS-07: the name of the condition that selects this flows edge (a name, never the expression)

target_from_content.$comment: ADR-093 FS-22: the call's URL or target is computed from conversation or tool data

cause.$comment: cause id from rules/causes.yaml (docs/03 §Causes); decorated from the loaded catalog, empty when the rule is not mapped

references.$comment: the rule's documentation references (ADR-095): decorated on read from the loaded catalog like cause, never a regulatory statement

remediation_framework.$comment: the rule's framework-native remediation for the finding's agent framework (ADR-093 decision 9): decorated on read against the architecture, never stored

provenance.description: Provenance sidecar (ADR-086, schema 1.1, docs/02 §Provenance): where each fact came from, keyed by an id-addressed JSON pointer as patches spell it (/nodes/<id>, /nodes/<id>/attrs/<key>, /edges/<id>/auth, /attrs/<key>; RFC 6901-escaped). The most specific key wins. Server-owned: a patch to /provenance is refused, an accepted import writes imported entries and an accepted patch resets each pointer it changes to declared with its actor. Rules never read it; they see the precomputed `prov` variable.
provenance.$comment: A node without an element-level entry resolves by the upgrade mapping of its source (design → declared, declared → imported, observed → observed) and the next save materialises it. `source` is written from the sidecar for two MINOR versions (ADR-040 §4). Every key and value passes the secret guard.

propertyNames.$comment: Every key must resolve to a model element, member or attribute under /nodes, /edges, /groups, /identities or /attrs: enforced in Go (invariant 9), which names the key's pointer and never echoes it.

provenanceKind.description: declared: typed by a person; imported: read from a source by an accepted import; observed: reserved, no ingestion path while OBSERVED_OVERLAY is off. Staleness is computed, never a kind.

provenanceActor.description: An actor id (user, agent key, service), never an e-mail address.

identifier.description: The source an imported fact was read from (file, export, registry), stable across re-imports; for a declared fact from a diagram import, the diagram.

hash.description: Hex SHA-256 of the source as read.

cadence_days.description: How often the source is expected to be read again; an imported fact is stale when now − fetched_at exceeds it (0: no cadence).

signature_verified.description: True only when the server verified a signature over the source; absent means false.

last_seen_import.description: Version or hash of the latest import of the identifier that still carried the fact; a later import that no longer carries it is drift.

path.$comment: RFC 6901 pointer; array segments under /nodes /edges /groups /findings may be an element id instead of an index

c4Level.$comment: ADR-032: C4 level of the element; empty = derived from the node type

c4Kind.$comment: ADR-032: C4 element kind; empty = derived from the node type

decision.$comment: ADR-032: an architecture decision record kept on the model; acceptance is a patch the user accepts, hence evidence
